tagline: Valley towns and farm roads lead to trails behind the falls.
intro: The Silver Falls Tour Route links Willamette Valley towns with vineyards, Christmas tree farms and the waterfalls of Silver Falls State Park. Oregon DOT presents this scenic route as a detour for I-5 travelers, covering 55 miles with a minimum driving time of two to three hours. On clear days, views include Mount Hood, Mount Adams, Mount Jefferson, Mount St. Helens and Mount Rainier.

The park at the heart of the drive emerged from a logged landscape. In 1902, Silverton photographer June D Drake began using his waterfall photographs to campaign for park status. A National Park Service inspector rejected the area in 1926 because logging had left so many stumps. Federal recreational development followed in 1935, and Civilian Conservation Corps workers built park facilities and the waterfall trail. Workers also widened natural passages behind the falls, making those recesses usable as public trails.

Start at the northern end in Woodburn and follow Oregon 214 southeast through Mt. Angel to Silverton. The highway continues to Silver Falls State Park, where the Canyon Trail passes ten waterfalls and runs behind several of them. Beyond the park, descend past the farms toward Sublimity, then continue through Turner to I-5 at Delaney Road south of Salem.

moments.title: Mount Angel Abbey
moments.text: Mount Angel Abbey occupies the top of a 485-foot butte, with a library designed by Finnish architect Alvar Aalto. Benedictine monks from Engelberg, Switzerland, founded the monastery in 1882. Mount Angel translates Engelberg into English; the city and butte took that name in 1883 through the efforts of Father Adelhelm Odermatt. Fire destroyed the second monastery in 1926, and the present monastery building was completed in 1928. The library came later, in 1970, and was renovated in 1980. Seminary and theology students use its collections. The collection includes medieval manuscripts dating to the twelfth century.

moments.title: Silverton
moments.text: Silverton's Four Freedoms murals are replacements, carrying Norman Rockwell's images onto a different building. The original murals stood at 402 Main Street until the building was razed in 2015; attempts to save them were abandoned, and they were destroyed during demolition. Community efforts produced a new replica at 990 North First Street. Silver Creek gives the town its name and runs through it from Silver Falls, linking the town geographically to the waterfalls farther along the drive. The town began downstream of Milford, an earlier community founded in 1846 with a sawmill, store and other buildings.
moments.notice: The Four Freedoms replica is at 990 North First Street.

moments.title: Silver Falls State Park
moments.text: At Silver Falls, erosion made room for a trail behind the water. Basalt flows covered older sandstone; the softer stone beneath wore away, leaving passages that Civilian Conservation Corps workers widened for public use. The Trail of Ten Falls passes behind South Falls, Lower South Falls, Middle North Falls and North Falls. South Falls drops 177 feet. Above it once stood the lumber town of Silver Falls City, where a local entrepreneur sold admission to attractions including cars pushed over the falls. For a shorter walk, a quarter-mile trail leads to Upper North Falls.
moments.notice: The trail passes behind four waterfalls, including South Falls.
